## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- Limited information is available about the shape of the bottom at this break.
- Limited information is available about this break's best season.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | Moderate | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |
| Swell size | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 1 disagrees. |
| Swell period | Moderate | Supported by one source (a surf magazine). |
| Wind | Moderate | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |
| Tide | Low | Supported by one source (a surf magazine); 4 disagree. |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Low | Described by one source (a surf magazine). |
| Season | Low | Supported by one source (a community source). |
| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 6 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Seven publishers, all read directly. Tide is still the main conflict. Yeeew is the only source that directly supports the profile's mid_to_high ('Works on a mid to high tide best'; the reef is 'best avoided at low'). Against it: WSL (Mid or Mid-low), Tourism Fiji ('All, but best at low'), WannaSurf (all tides, rising) and the Tavarua resort (all tides, skill-dependent). Tourism Fiji also notes that higher tides make it less scary. Wind is well supported: SE (Yeeew), SE/E (WannaSurf) and ESE trades offshore (Perfect Wave Travel), all within 15 deg of the profile's 120. WSL's table line 'Light S to SSE 5-10kts or light/variable' is not called offshore or best and includes light/variable, so it is recorded with no offshore value. It no longer counts against the profile. Size disagrees at the top end. WSL (3-6 ft) and the Tavarua resort (2-6 ft) give maximums well below the profile's 10 ft. WannaSurf (3-10 ft+) and Yeeew (waist high to double overhead) agree with it. The 6 ft figures may be back-measured local sizes, so this may be a scale difference rather than a real conflict. Seasonality gap filled: Perfect Wave Travel says the swells Restaurants needs are rare from November to April, which matches a May-October season. The profile also includes April. Period: WSL's 11-15 s is still the only number. Bathymetry is qualitative only (shallow coral reef). No peer-reviewed or survey source mentions Restaurants, and Surf-Forecast has no Restaurants page. The WSL URL without its slug opens the same 2015 post as the Cloudbreak source, and its table covers both breaks.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 3 ft [S1] · 2 ft [S6] · waist high [S5] (scale not stated) / surfer heights | conflicting | S1, S5, S6 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | waist high to double overhead · surfer heights (face) | documented | S5 | no separate setting; working range 3–10 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 6 ft [S1, S6] · double overhead [S5] (scale not stated) / surfer heights | conflicting | S1, S5, S6 | `wave_height_max_ft` 10 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WSL's table gives a swell size of 3-6 ft and the Tavarua resort says it breaks from 2 ft, neither saying whether these are faces or back-measured sizes, while Yeeew says it gets good from waist high, a face height relative to the surfer.
  - S1 (World Surf League): “Swell size: 3-6'”
  - S6 (Tavarua Island Resort): “it can break in the 2ft - 6ft range”
  - S5 (Yeeew!): “Gets good between waist-high and double overhead.”
- **Ideal range**: Yeeew says it gets good between waist high and double overhead, a face height relative to the surfer with no number in feet; WSL's 3-6 ft table size is not called ideal.
  - S5 (Yeeew!): “Gets good between waist-high and double overhead.”
- **Maximum suitable**: WSL and the Tavarua resort both top out at 6 ft without stating the scale, while Yeeew says it is still good at double overhead (face height), which may be a scale difference rather than a real disagreement; Tourism Fiji, Yeeew, the resort and Perfect Wave add only that it is smaller than Cloudbreak.
  - S1 (World Surf League): “Swell size: 3-6'”
  - S6 (Tavarua Island Resort): “it can break in the 2ft - 6ft range”
  - S5 (Yeeew!): “Gets good between waist-high and double overhead.”

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: All four directional sources include southwest (225 deg): WSL gives SSW to SW, WannaSurf West and SouthWest, Yeeew South and Southwest, and Perfect Wave says best with solid SW groundswell.
  - S1 (World Surf League): “Swell Direction: SSW to SW”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Good swell directionWest, SouthWest”
  - S5 (Yeeew!): “The best swells are from the South and Southwest.”
  - S7 (Perfect Wave Travel): “Best with solid SW groundswell”
- **Acceptable range**: The span runs from Yeeew's South through WSL's SSW-SW to WannaSurf's West, the union of the directions the sources call best or good; no source states an explicit window.
  - S5 (Yeeew!): “The best swells are from the South and Southwest.”
  - S1 (World Surf League): “Swell Direction: SSW to SW”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Good swell directionWest, SouthWest”
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names swell directions that are blocked or shadowed by land or reefs.
- **Exposure**: Tourism Fiji says it does not catch as much swell, Yeeew and the Tavarua resort say it is a bit or normally smaller than Cloudbreak, and Perfect Wave says it is often epic at half Cloudbreak's size.
  - S2 (Tourism Fiji (fiji.travel)): “It doesn't catch as much swell, but it breaks as perfectly as a wave pool”
  - S5 (Yeeew!): “When Cloudbreak is maxed out, Restaurants is the place to be as it's always a bit smaller.”
  - S6 (Tavarua Island Resort): “It's normally smaller than Cloudbreak and can offer a machine-like generated wave of perfection that screams down the line.”
  - S7 (Perfect Wave Travel): “when Cloudbreak is huge, Restaurants is often epic at half the size!”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: WSL's table gives a swell size of 3-6 ft and the Tavarua resort says it breaks from 2 ft, neither saying whether these are faces or back-measured sizes, while Yeeew says it gets good from waist high, a face height relative to the surfer.
- **Swell height · maximum suitable**: WSL and the Tavarua resort both top out at 6 ft without stating the scale, while Yeeew says it is still good at double overhead (face height), which may be a scale difference rather than a real disagreement; Tourism Fiji, Yeeew, the resort and Perfect Wave add only that it is smaller than Cloudbreak.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: WSL says mid or mid-low and Tourism Fiji all tides but best at low, while Yeeew says mid to high and that the shallow reef is best avoided at low, and WannaSurf and the Tavarua resort say all tides.
